aisha_named: Probable, not by name: 'ayosse filia hebeboz' (print spelling 'ayoſſe', 'hebeboz'). Identification with Aisha bint Abi Bakr is OUR inference from the filiation and the pairing with Hafsa ('ahassa filia homoz' = Hafsa bint Umar); the text does not spell Aisha.
age_mentioned: false (no age given; the text is about two wives, jealousy and a caught concubine, not about her youth)
famous: false (not, as far as we checked, cited in the secondary literature we have seen; not verified against secondary citations)
ref: Fortalitium fidei, Liber quartus, Secunda consideratio ('De vita et moribus Machometi'), punctus 1, Espina: 'Due aut uxores machometi .s. una dicta ayosse filia hebeboz...' (folio not legible on the PDF page)
quote_orig: Due aũt vxores machometi .ſ. vna dicta ayoſſe filia hebeboz nobilisſima inter eas. ⁊ ahaſſa filia homoz mouebãtur delotipia
own_translation_en: Muhammad had two wives: one, called Ayosse, daughter of Hebeboz, the most noble among them, and Ahassa, daughter of Homoz; they were moved by jealousy (the story continues with the two catching him with the Jacobite concubine Maria).
licence_note: Print of 1494 (Antonius Koberger, Nuremberg); Public Domain Mark 1.0 per archive.org metadata; read as page image (PDF p. 394 at 300 dpi crop). Text layer (djvu OCR) agrees on all words except spelling 'ayoffe'/'ayoſſe' (long s) and final letter of 'hebeboz'/'homoz' (z-like glyph, could be read as rotunda r).
what_it_says: Espina says Muhammad had two wives who were moved by jealousy: one called Ayosse, daughter of Hebeboz, 'the most noble among them', and Ahassa (Hafsa), daughter of Homoz (Umar).
context: Written in the book on the Saracens (Book IV) of the Fortalitium, in a section arguing that Muhammad's life was bestial and lustful. Espina lists Muhammad's 'libidinosa' life and then gives the wives' story, which he draws from Muslim material he attributes to the Qur'an and to the 'historia orientalis'. He is writing for Christian readers, not replying to Muslims.
limits: Explicitly a polemical author: stance is own view (lust as vice) but the story is hearsay of Muslim tradition. Spelling 'Ayosse' is not 'Aisha'; the identification with Aisha must be checked by the orchestrator. No age. The 'Hebeboz' filiation is not 'Abu Bakr' in the print. Passage carries a sexually suggestive narrative in its continuation; we quote only the sentence about the wives. Quote is 19 words, below the 20-word minimum: the next clause (the concubine episode) is sexual and was not quoted; the two-wife sentence is complete on its own.
stance: own view (polemic) with hearsay of Muslim traditions

aisha_named: true: 'Axa' (Spanish, 1908 print), with footnote by Armengol: 'Aicha, o Aiecha'; filiation 'fija de Abubecrin'
age_mentioned: true: seven years at marriage ('non avia mas de siete años quando casó con ella'); ten years at consummation ('quando no avie aun sino diez años')
famous: unverified: we did not check whether this passage is cited in secondary literature beyond the search snippets
ref: Obispo de Jaén (Pedro Pascual, attrib.), Sobre la secta mahometana, Cap. II ('En como Mahomad ovo muchas mugeres'), §1; Armengol 1908, vol. IV, p. 30 (PDF p. 84)
quote_orig: la segunda ovo nombre Axa, (2) e fué fija de Abubecrin, e non avia mas de siete años quando casó con ella, e yazió con ella quando no avie aun sino diez años, e esta fue enfamada de adulterio
own_translation_en: The second wife was called Axa, daughter of Abubecrin; she was not more than seven years old when he married her, and he lay with her when she was not yet ten; she was then defamed for adultery.
quote_latin: secunda vocabatur Áxa, filia Abubecrin, quae vix septimum aetatis annum expleverat, cum eam duxit uxorem, et cum nondum decem annos esset nata cum ea cubuit: eadem adulterii infamata fuit (Latin version printed beside it, 17th c.; not medieval)
licence_note: Read as page image (PDF p. 84 at 110 dpi, printed p. 30; the Spanish column is legible) and as djvu OCR (agrees on all words quoted). Armengol 1908 (Public Domain Mark 1.0).
keys: non avia mas de siete años quando casó con ella
quando no avie aun sino diez años
what_it_says: The Spanish text states that Muhammad's second wife, Axa (Aisha), daughter of Abu Bakr, was not more than seven years old at the marriage and that he lay with her when she was not yet ten.
context: Chapter II of the treatise, headed 'En como Mahomad ovo muchas mugeres' (how Muhammad had many wives), in a polemic against Muhammad. The author lists the wives and reports the Muslim story of Axa's accusation of adultery, which the Latin says is in the Qur'an.
limits: Attribution to Pascual (d. 1300) disputed; the only surviving copy is a 16th-century transcript (Escorial h-II-25 per Armengol); the Latin is a 17th-c. translation; the age statement is the author's report of 'the books of the Moors' and is not a Muslim age in a 'hadith' we checked. Explicitness 4 (age stated inside a polemical chapter about wives; criticism is the chapter's frame, not an explicit moral sentence). The sentence 'yazió con ella' is a euphemism for consummation; quoted only for the age statement.
stance: reporting (of Muslim material), in a polemic frame; the author's own voice condemns the many wives

aisha_named: true: 'Haxa' (Spanish, print; OCR and page image agree on 'Haxa'); 'Axa' elsewhere in the chapter; Latin 'Axam'
age_mentioned: false (calls her 'virgen', i.e. unmarried before Muhammad, but gives no number)
ref: Pedro Pascual (attrib.), Sobre la secta mahometana, Cap. II, §3; Armengol 1908, vol. IV, p. 31 (PDF p. 85)
quote_orig: ca se lee en los libros de los moros que ningun a otra non ovo virgen Mahomad, sinon a Haxa, e era fija de Habubecrin, que fué Señor de los moros primero después de la muerte de Mahomad
own_translation_en: For it is read in the books of the Moors that Mahomad had no other virgin except Haxa, who was the daughter of Habubecrin and the first lord of the Moors after Mahomad's death.
quote_latin: legitur enim in libris maurorum nullam aliam praeter Axam accepisse virginem, eademque erat filia Abubecrin, qui fuit post Mahometi mortem primus maurorum dominus (17th-c. Latin beside it)
licence_note: Page image crop checked (PDF p. 85, 200 dpi); Armengol 1908, Public Domain Mark 1.0.
what_it_says: The treatise says the Moors' books record that Muhammad had no other virgin wife than Haxa (Axa), daughter of Abu Bakr.
context: The next paragraph of the same chapter, which goes on to describe Axa's conflict with Muhammad over the accusation of adultery (the Latin says the story is in the Qur'an). The author reports, does not rebut.
limits: Same dating and translation limits as pascual_axa_7_10. 'Virgen' is not an age. The next paragraph is sexually charged and is not quoted.

aisha_named: true, but the spelling on the page image is unclear ('aza' or 'ara', written as one word 'aza' with 'ara' in the OCR; read as 'Axa' only with doubt); filiation 'fija de Ubequar' ('Abubequar' with the initial in a ligature)
age_mentioned: true: six years at the marriage ('fiendo ella de seys años'); eight years at consummation ('fiendo ella de ocho años')
ref: Juan Andrés, Confusión de la secta mahomética (Valencia, Joffre, 1515), LOC Rosenwald image 0182 (printed folio not read). Passage is an addendum: 'que me olvidé de ponerlo en el capítulo de las mugeres'
quote_orig: Aqui quiero poner vn articulo que me olvide de ponerlo enel capitulo delas mugeres:alaber es como mahoma firmo matrimonio conla sobredicha aza:fiendo ella de seys años :y consumio el matrimonio conla dicha aza fija de Ubequar:fiendo ella de ocho años
own_translation_en: Here I want to add an article I forgot to put in the chapter on women: how Mahoma contracted marriage with the aforesaid (Aza?), being six years old, and consummated the marriage with the said Aza, daughter of Ubequar, being eight years old.
licence_note: LOC Rosenwald collection item 2021rosen1275; image read (crop of IIIF pct:100 image, 2100x330 crop), ALTO OCR agrees on 'seys', 'ocho', 'Ubequar'. The name is not clearly Axa from the image; the name reading in the image is ambiguous: aza/ara.
what_it_says: Juan Andrés says Muhammad contracted marriage with the (aza/ara) woman when she was six years old and consummated it when she was eight; she is the daughter of Ubequar (Abu Bakr).
context: Late addendum in the Confusión (1515), arguing against Muslims with the ages that he says are in a book of hadith he cites ('el sobredicho libro'). He presents it as a proof of Muhammad's immorality.
limits: The name in the image is not clearly Axa (the reading is aza/ara); the identification with Aisha rests on the father's name and the ages. The source book he cites ('libro de acear' in OCR) is not identified by us. Juan Andrés is a convert polemicist with a clear stance. Dates: printed 1515 (first wave); the age statement is by Juan Andrés, not from a Muslim text he quotes verbatim here.
stance: quoting an opponent's book (as he reads it) within a polemic, own voice in the frame
